subject: The fitted-bedroom journey from measure to installation
hook: Four steps from bare wall to fitted wardrobe
ig:
A fitted wardrobe is four steps, and knowing what each one needs from you makes the whole thing easier.

1. Design consultation. Free, no obligation. The most useful thing you can bring is an honest list of what you actually store: how many long coats, how many pairs of shoes, where the suitcases live.

2. Measure and itemised quote. We survey the room properly, including skirting, sockets, the ceiling line and how the bedroom door swings. You then get a quote that lists every section and fitting, so nothing is hidden.

3. Workshop build. Your wardrobe is cut, edged, drilled and assembled in our own workshop in Hanley, then checked before it goes on the van. It is never flat-pack.

4. Installation. Our own team fits it, levels it, scribes it to your walls and aligns the doors.

Save this so you know what to prepare, then tap the link in bio to see our fitted wardrobes.
fb:
Thinking about fitted wardrobes but not sure what the process actually looks like? Here it is, start to finish.

It begins with a free, no-obligation chat about what you need to store. Then we measure the room properly — walls, skirting, sockets, the lot — and send an itemised quote so you can see exactly what you are paying for.

Once you are happy, everything is built in our workshop in Hanley, Stoke-on-Trent, and checked before it leaves. Our own team then fits it, levelling and scribing it to your walls.

Swipe through for what to have ready at each stage, and have a look at our fitted wardrobes here:
